what: The owner's free-text verdicts on the TaoMate-H3 probe arms and audio-freeze arms (docs/h3_taomate.md section 4, steps 1 and 2).
judged_by: the owner, and the people the owner showed the clips to

renders.pdd8_freeze_clips_compared: the 2026-09-12 renders named in the freeze manifest's compare_against_existing

owner_words: everyone has said the pdd is like 100x better than any of the taomates and i'd agree. im not sure i can tell any difference between kijai's and ours taomates... but pdd is 100x better.
in the dancer videos, she morphs into 2 people.
the voice frozen is the only good taomate.
all the diner scenes are washed out and have things morphing/cloning for taomate. just bad. pdd is 100x better by everyone i showed it to in every scene.

verdicts.taomate_vs_pdd8: PDD8 far better in every scene, by the owner and by everyone the owner showed the clips to
verdicts.ours_vs_kijai: no difference the owner can tell
verdicts.diner_taomate: washed out, with things morphing and cloning
verdicts.dancer_taomate_frozen: the dancer morphs into two people
verdicts.dancer_taomate_loose: the dancer morphs into two people
verdicts.voice_taomate_frozen: good: the only good TaoMate render

consistent_with: The ours-vs-kijai verdict matches the stored-weight measurement bench/results/2026-09-15_merge_noise_taomate.json, where per-cast requantisation noise exceeds the gap between the two files in every module. The verdict does not test that measurement.
is_not: A blind or seeded distribution. It is one seed per scene, judged in free text after seeing which arm was which. Nothing here isolates a cause. docs/h3_taomate.md section 3 lists what a ComfyUI graph changes from the authors' runtime; whole-clip denoising with no causal chunks or clean K/V cache is the most direct candidate for morphing and cloning, but that is reasoned, not measured.
consequence: No further TaoMate renders are scheduled. Step 3 (the trajectory freeze patch) and step 4 (the lever arms) are not run, and the lane is parked until the owner reopens it.
